children: The dollar index rose to 99.3 on Friday, rebounding from a two-week low after stronger-than-expected US employment data bolstered expectations for tighter monetary policy.
US nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August, following an upwardly revised gain of 23,000 in July and well above market expectations for a 56,000 increase.
Meanwhile, the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, while annual wage growth eased to 3.1%, although the decline was smaller than markets had anticipated.
Money markets are now pricing in a near 58% probability of a rate hike in September, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

title: Dollar Rebounds on Stronger-Than-Expected US Jobs Data
